Oct 10 : New Zealand fast-bowler Will O'Rourke will miss the series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from injuries to his left hamstring and calf, the country's cricket board said on Saturday. O'Rourke suffered a hamstring tear during New Zealand's test series win over England in June, before hurting his calf in training in late August. The 25-year-old will aim to return to full fitness ahead of a four-test tour of neighbours Australia beginning on December 9. "It's obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India," New Zealand coach Rob Walter said in a statement.

"Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we're taking a conservative approach to Will's return to ensure he's fully fit before he takes the field again." New Zealand host India in five Twenty20 internationals, five one-day internationals and two tests, with the opening T20 in Christchurch on October 22.

US says China's maritime actions off Taiwan 'deeply destabilising'

"By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek," a US State Department spokesperson said.

FAST

TAIPEI: China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tension, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters in August. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, say they believe China is practicing for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets. Taipei regards the area off its east coast as critical to wartime supply routes from allies in the event of a blockade or conflict.

The United States remains concerned by China's activity east of Taiwan, a State Department spokesperson said, responding to a question on the sighting of the militia boat. "China's actions are deeply destabilising," the spokesperson added. "By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek." The US urges Beijing to cease its pressure against Taiwan and instead engage in "meaningful dialogue with Taiwan's democratically elected authorities", the spokesperson added. China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over waters surrounding it. The US is Taiwan's most important international backer, though President Donald Trump has yet to approve a new US$14 billion arms sale package for the island. Taiwan's Coast Guard said in a statement about the militia boat and its accompanying vessels that their activities were all located outside of "restricted waters". In a practice dating to the 1950s, China's maritime militia, more commonly seen around South China Sea flashpoints, consists of fishing vessels whose crews receive training and support to operate in disputed waters, often alongside coast guard ships. In June, Britain, France, Germany and the US, all expressed concern over Chinese activities off Taiwan's east coast as a threat to regional stability and freedom of navigation.

Source: Reuters/cf

Oct 10 : Cole Palmer remains committed to playing for England, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insisted after the attacker drew criticism for missing the international break due to injury. Palmer, left out of England's World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin injury affected his form, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for Nations League fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia. However, Palmer was forced to pull out of the squad due to a recurrence of the issue, with Tuchel saying the 24-year-old "misses too many opportunities" to play in an England shirt. Asked about Tuchel's comments on Friday, Alonso told reporters: "The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he is feeling OK.

FAST

NEW DELHI: Central Delhi was sealed on Saturday (Oct 10), with thousands of police and paramilitaries on patrol, metro stations shut, mobile internet suspended and markets closed to guard against a youth protest demanding India's chief election officer quit. The protest, called by the "Cockroach" youth movement, hopes to draw thousands of demonstrators who want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to quit over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. Touted by the organisers as a protest to "Save Democracy", it aims to be the biggest of the demonstrations that were launched last week after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's deputies had questioned and disagreed with him over the revision process that saw some 130 million voter names removed. Opposition parties have long alleged that the government is trying to fix voter lists to its advantage and were quick to resurrect the allegations following the report.

Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations. NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The BJP says Modi's popularity and India's economic growth are some key reasons for its electoral dominance and that opposition parties are misleading the country as they are unable to win elections. Nonetheless, the near daily protests by opposition groups pose a new political challenge to Modi, just months after similar demonstrations forced his education minister to quit over exam paper leaks.

Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra attend a protest organized by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Oct 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Adnan Abidi)

It also comes months before a series of key state elections starting in early 2027, including in the BJP-ruled most populous state of Uttar Pradesh. The protesters, led by the self-named "Cockroach Janta Party", that began as an online satire, have said they will gather at Jantar Mantar - a site designated for protests by authorities in the heart of New Delhi - at 10 am. (0430 GMT). FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT TO PROTEST, CJP SAYS Delhi Police said on Friday that they had not given permission for the protest as the request did not come on time, CJP had violated undertakings given during previous protests, and that authorities had to enforce the law and maintain peace. Police also said protesters would face the force of the law if they violated the ban. CJP leaders rejected the police decision and said they would go ahead with the protest as it was their fundamental right. In what is seen as a bid to thwart protesters arriving in Delhi and the central business district where Jantar Mantar is located, several long-distance trains to the city were cancelled on Friday and 57 metro stations shut from Friday night. Mobile internet services in a radius of 4 km (2.5 miles) of the protest area were ordered suspended from Friday night to Saturday night, ANI news agency reported citing a government order.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 9 : Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising. Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.  The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change. Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.

Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones.  The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said. Nuvacore declined to comment. The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021. Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned. Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand. Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data. Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts. Shares in both companies have risen more than 180 per cent this year. Nvidia launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to sell $20 billion worth of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

Source: Reuters
